summary: Odd Lots interview with commodity hedge fund manager Pierre Andurand on his long cocoa, copper and oil theses, May 2024. Approach is fundamental supply-demand balance modelling with stocks-to-grindings ratio, high-frequency export tracking, inelastic demand and slow supply response; also discusses positioning, liquidity and why pod funds miss multi-year deficits.

claims.speaker: Joe Weisenthal
claims.quote: you can have like solid bullish fundamentals and the price
claims.claim: Even with a market in deficit and bullish fundamentals, prices can correct sharply because trees do not grow to the sky; cocoa had surged above 11,000 then fell to about 8,000.
claims.testable: partly - price corrections vs fundamentals are observable

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: I have one analyst who very good and who in January Pi you should look at CoCo
claims.claim: Andurand, mainly an energy and metals trader, entered cocoa because an analyst proposed it, and then both dug deep into fundamentals to build a thesis outside his usual markets.

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: most analysts out there have it down 11% but that's because they tend to be very conservative you know they have lot of clients and they don't want to worry the world
claims.claim: Andurand sees cocoa production down about 17.7% versus the consensus of 11% because sell-side analysts give conservative estimates to avoid alarming clients, so consensus lags a supply shock.
claims.conditions: when own tracking of exports diverges from consensus

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: really tracking the export from the the main exporters mainly Ivory Coast and Ghana that wees together about 60% of world's production
claims.claim: Tracking exports of Ivory Coast and Ghana (about 60% of world supply) showed shipments down 30% and 41% year to date, a direct high-frequency read on the supply deficit.
claims.indicator: Ivory Coast and Ghana cocoa port exports

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: that represent only 20% of the balance of the season for West Africa and and that's not going to be enough to to really change the deficit that we have this year
claims.claim: The mid-crop represents only about 20% of the rest of the season so it cannot close the roughly 800,000 ton deficit (about 5 million ton market).

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: at first you eat into current inventories until you run out of inventories and then the price can go anywhere
claims.claim: A supply deficit is first absorbed by drawing inventories, and once inventories run out price has no ceiling and must rise until demand is destroyed.

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: demand is extremely inelastic I mean you can study that historically when you have a recession or not when prices go up a lot or not I mean demand generally goes up
claims.claim: Cocoa demand is extremely inelastic historically, so the price was capped at $2,500-3,000 by supply, not demand, and a supply shortfall must be cleared by price alone.

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: people consume 1.7 grams of cocoa per day which at $110,000 a ton represents 1.7 Cent per day
claims.claim: Back-of-envelope: 5 million tons of demand over 8 billion people means a few cents per person per day even at very high cocoa prices, so higher prices barely hit consumers' budgets and do not cut consumption.
claims.indicator: cocoa cost as share of consumer spending
claims.conditions: cocoa content in chocolate small (milk chocolate under 10%)
claims.testable: yes - arithmetic on demand and price

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: 70% in West Africa and then you have a 21% in main Latin America and 5% in Asia and Oceania
claims.claim: Cocoa production is concentrated near a latitude band needing specific temperature, rainfall and humidity: 70% West Africa, 21% Latin America, 5% Asia and Oceania, so local shocks hit global supply.

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: some of it due to El Nino we had um basically period of time when when it was too hot and period of time when we had way way too much rain
claims.claim: El Nino caused heat and excess rain that cut the cocoa crop, and La Nina next year should help at the margin, making part of the shortfall cyclical.
claims.conditions: El Nino hurts West African cocoa, La Nina helps

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: climate change is every year Shifting the weather patterns generally unfavorably for Coco Productions
claims.claim: Climate change steadily shifts weather patterns unfavorably for cocoa, a structural drag on supply that does not reverse with a good season.
claims.testable: partly - hard to separate from cycle

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: a tree that has that swollen Sho disease loses 25% yield within the first last year and 50% within two years and the tree dies within 3 to four years
claims.claim: Swollen shoot virus (known since 1936, spread by mealybugs) cuts yield 25% in a year and 50% in two and kills trees in 3 to 4 years; its spread over the last year is a structural supply loss.

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: black pot disease that that come from a fungus and it occurs mainly during the rainy season it's spread by by rain splash
claims.claim: Black pod fungus spreads by rain splash in wet seasons, so heavy rain such as in El Nino years raises disease losses.

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: less usage of fertilizers mainly in Ivory Coast due to high fertilizer prices and and also shortages due to the Russian invasion of Ukraine
claims.claim: Ivory Coast farmers used less fertilizer due to high prices and Russia-Ukraine shortages, cutting yields; it will not reverse soon because farmers still receive low prices.

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: the farmers are still getting relatively low prices and they're still struggling to make and meat
claims.claim: Farmer-gate prices stayed low, so farmers cannot afford inputs and no supply response from fertilizer is expected: Andurand sees the supply problems as largely structural rather than weather.

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: you have some Consultants that are specialized and every month they have a team doing surveys of the main produc regions
claims.claim: Even in a less transparent market, specialist consultants survey the main producing regions monthly, giving enough data to forecast next year's crop.

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: they believe okay the top of the range is a high price for Apple but they don't really ask themselves what makes that price right
claims.claim: Experienced traders anchor on the historical price range and do not ask what price is needed to balance the market; stepping back to compute the balancing price gives an edge.
claims.conditions: after structural change in supply response

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: would have the supply response if prices were going up but if now you get you don't get the supply response or the supply response takes four or five years then you need to have a demand response
claims.claim: If a price rise no longer triggers a quick supply response (cocoa trees take 4-5 years), the market can clear only through demand, requiring a much larger price rise.
claims.direction: long when supply response is delayed
claims.testable: partly - lag between price and supply

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: previous High in 1977 was 5,500 something doll a ton of $1 1977 which is equivalent to $28,000 a ton of today's dollar
claims.claim: Judged in real terms, the 1977 cocoa peak equals about $28,000 a ton today, so the nominal 'all-time high' headline overstates how stretched prices are.

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: you have to like look at a bit more history and and understand in the past how prices reacted to a shortage how long it took to recover
claims.claim: Use historical shortages to see how prices reacted and how long supply took to recover, then adjust for what is different today.

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: there's a ratio that we look at that most people look at it's actually the inventory to to grinding ratio so it's it's a measure of inventory to demand
claims.claim: The key balance indicator is the stocks-to-grindings ratio (inventory divided by industrial processing demand).

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: grindings look to be down three three and a half% this year despite the fact that the end demand is the same in volume
claims.claim: Grindings fell 3-3.5% while chocolate demand was flat in volume, meaning destocking at every level of the chain (beans, butter, powder), which hides how short the market is.

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: now we have the largest deficit ever on top of two previous years of deficit and it looks like next year we will have a deficit
claims.claim: A record deficit after two earlier deficit years, and another expected, puts the stocks-to-grindings ratio around 21% versus 35-40% in the last decade.

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: at 19% and that's what drove us to $28,000 a ton of today's dollars
claims.claim: In 1977 a 19% stocks-to-grindings ratio drove cocoa to about $28,000 in today's dollars, the historical analogue for the current 21%.
claims.direction: long cocoa at very low ratio

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: if we have another deficit next year then we we might go down to 13%
claims.claim: Another deficit year would push the ratio to about 13%, an outright shortage of beans where price must explode since demand cannot be slowed.

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: if you have no physical somebody wants to take delivery the price can go anywhere so it's a dangerous commodity to short
claims.claim: Physically settled futures converge to the physical price, so with no physical available shorts face unbounded squeezes.

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: the fonts have been selling since February they actually went from a a length of 175,000 Lots
claims.claim: Funds (speculators) cut longs by more than 80% from 175,000 lots to 28,000 since February, so the cocoa rally was not fund-driven; claims that funds pushed prices were untrue.
claims.indicator: speculative fund net long in cocoa futures (COT)

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: the people who've been buying futures from the fonts it's producers because they're producing a lot less than
claims.claim: Producers who had sold forward were buying back futures from funds because their crops fell short of expectations, a source of buying not seen in positioning headlines.

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: and then we get into a market where you have less liquidity because you have less exposure you have less Longs and less less shorts and then the Vol volatility increases
claims.claim: As the price moved massively, open interest shrank, liquidity thinned and volatility rose, causing traders to cut position sizes, which in turn makes prices even more volatile.
claims.testable: yes - open interest and vol data

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: you have to calibrate your position to to be able to take a 50% move Mo against you on the way
claims.claim: In an illiquid, volatile commodity size so that a 50% adverse move can be survived; being right on direction is not enough.
claims.conditions: illiquid market with large deficit and low inventories

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: you have to be out completely because I still think that there's more upside than downside I think we still have the potential to go above $20,000 a ton later this year
claims.claim: Andurand stayed long cocoa with about $2,000 downside (December contract $7,000 to $5,000) versus $13-15k upside (over $20,000), a skewed payoff.
claims.testable: no - single view, time-bound to May 2024

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: for that you need a lot of things need to go right you need like a bumper crop in West Africa next year
claims.claim: The bearish scenario needs a bumper West African crop and near-perfect weather for the rest of the year, so the probability of a drop is not zero but low.

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: if we have the production going back up roughly 10% from this year to next year we still have a deficit of 300,000 tons or so next year
claims.claim: Even a 10% production rebound leaves a deficit of about 300,000 tons next year, bringing the ratio to about 13%, far below 1977.

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: then the prices will probably come off from here towards you know I don't know five or $6,000 a ton
claims.claim: If surveys over the next four months show a great Ivory Coast and Ghana crop, the price should fall toward $5-6k but not back to $2,500.
claims.indicator: crop surveys of Ivory Coast and Ghana
claims.direction: exit cocoa on strong crop surveys
claims.testable: partly - surveys are a leading indicator

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: because we need we have a very low inventory so we need to rebuild stocks everywhere
claims.claim: Because inventories are very low, prices cannot drop back to old levels; stocks must be rebuilt across the supply chain, which keeps a demand floor.

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: in Europe only 20% of the the inventories on Exchange 20% of the European stocks are on Exchange the others are really with with the chocolate makers
claims.claim: Cocoa inventory data are partial: US stocks are on exchange but only 20% of European stocks are; port stocks in Ivory Coast and Ghana are visible, and specialist firms estimate the rest with cross-validation.

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: you have this underlying climate change that is also a trend that really impact production over time
claims.claim: Beyond random weather, climate change creates a trending structural impact on soft commodity production that offers theme opportunities beyond cocoa.
claims.testable: partly - hard to separate from weather

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: three to five years for that Cocoa Tree to give you cocoa beans
claims.claim: Tree crops take 3-5 years to respond to price versus immediate replanting for grains, so supply response is slow.

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: so it should makees make it easier in a way to have position that you can hold for longer that are a bit more structural than than for GRS
claims.claim: Because supply responds slowly, shocks create larger and longer moves in cocoa than in grains, making it easier to hold structural positions.
claims.conditions: tree crops with slow supply response

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: versus Coco where you have many one Mega major producer and another very large one
claims.claim: Cocoa is easier to analyze than grains because production is concentrated in one mega producer and one large producer, so a few data points give a good read on next year's crop.

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: demand was growing about half a million ton a year and Supply was growing half a million ton a year in average
claims.claim: For 15-20 years copper was balanced, with demand and supply each growing about 0.5 million tons a year.

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: Renewables take a lot more copper than like nuclear plants or like fossil fuel generated electricity
claims.claim: Electrification of transport, grid expansion for renewables (solar, wind) and data centers add new copper demand, much copper-intensive versus nuclear or fossil power.

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: we see Market in which we are going to have overall 1 million tons of demand per year roughly of demand increase per year and the supply growth basically by the end of next year will be zero to negative
claims.claim: Despite weaker Chinese property demand, copper demand grows about 1 million tons a year while mine supply growth goes to zero or negative within 12-18 months, producing a widening multi-year deficit.

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: a bunch of like pods that have very many many teams in in those big multi strategy funds that have very tight draw Downs so they tend to try to trade for the next few days
claims.claim: Copper has not priced the coming deficit because most hedge fund capital sits in multi-strategy pods with tight drawdown limits that cannot hold positions beyond days or weeks, so the market gives no early price signal to fix a multi-year deficit.
claims.direction: long-horizon investors can earn the deficit premium
claims.testable: partly - structural claim about market participants

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: if you bring a new mine it's like more than 10 years to bring it's like 10 to 15 years to bring a new mine
claims.claim: New copper mines take 10-15 years and growth is shifting to less stable countries, so supply cannot respond quickly to price.

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: the price of copper is a very small percentage of the price of the end product right so if copper goes up 10 times I mean your end product will go up a little bit
claims.claim: Copper demand is inelastic because copper is a small fraction of end-product cost and the energy transition must proceed regardless of price, so the price move needed to balance the market is large.

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: we look at it year year by year so so we think okay at current prices what would be the supply and demand balance
claims.claim: Method for a fair price: model supply and demand year by year at current prices, assess price sensitivity of each side, and treat the price path (not a single price) as the question.

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: when prices go up you get more scrap Supply that that comes as a source of supply for copper
claims.claim: Scrap supply is the only quick supply response to higher copper prices, while mine supply does not respond for years; demand shifting to later is limited.

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: we're going to get about like 400 to 500,000 tons deficit and we had less than that in terms of visible stocks at the beginning of the year
claims.claim: Projected 2024 deficit of 400-500k tons exceeds visible stocks, so visible inventories could run out by year-end.

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: if they know that we're going to at the beginning of a multi-year deficit they're not going to sell their strategic reserves in the first year
claims.claim: China's strategic reserve (SRB) is an extra inventory but would not be sold early in a multi-year deficit, so it cannot cap prices.

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: deficit that are more than a million tons and eventually more than 3 million tons in 2030
claims.claim: Deficits accumulate to more than 1 million tons in 2026 and over 3 million tons by 2030, exceeding inventory buffers.

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: we're going to have to have a non nonlinear move sooner than later because of the large deficit
claims.claim: With a large deficit, low inventories and inelastic demand, copper must move non-linearly to force demand destruction, possibly a multiple of the price rather than 20%.

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: I think they could go up four times so know over 5 year 5 year Horizon
claims.claim: Andurand sees copper potentially quadrupling over a five-year horizon, since a 20% move would not change the supply-demand balance.

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: we all expecting to see at least some decline in Russian production due to sanctions or due to issues in Russia and and at the end we there was no no Supply response at all
claims.claim: Expected oil supply disruptions in 2022-23 (Russia sanctions, Iran) did not materialize: Russian output held, Iranian exports surged on weak enforcement and US supply grew faster than expected, so consensus overestimated disruption.

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: I mean is US shell production about to Peak or not we don't know we'll only know it after the fact
claims.claim: US shale growth has disappointed over the last four months, which may be the start of a peak but four months is not yet a trend.

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: if the conflict stays between Israel and Gaza I mean there's no oil there it has no impact at all on o o oil supply
claims.claim: Real supply loss would need an attack on Iranian oil facilities, prompting Iran to hit Saudi facilities or close Hormuz, which is low probability; the Gaza conflict alone has no oil supply impact.

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: the ukrainians have not attacked pipelines and ports yet I think if they really wanted to to impact the revenues of Russia they should attack the ports
claims.claim: Ukrainian strikes have hit Russian refineries not ports or crude pipelines, which would be the way to cut Russian revenue and would impact supply.

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: the Biden Administration is very very paranoid about having high gasoline prices before the election
claims.claim: The US pressures Ukraine not to hit Russian ports before the election to avoid high gasoline prices, but a more desperate Ukraine might attack them, creating a supply-disruption risk.

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: it's just a question of geology and and money actually more than anything
claims.claim: US oil supply growth is set by geology and capital rather than who is president, and US output is probably near peak, so the election matters marginally for production.

claims.speaker: Pierre Andurand
claims.quote: I would expect Trump to enforce the sanctions on Iran more tightly so we might lose some oil from Iran
claims.claim: A Trump presidency would probably enforce Iran sanctions more tightly, removing some Iranian oil, partly offset by more Saudi supply, so overall effect on oil prices is small.

claims.speaker: Tracy Alaway
claims.quote: if everyone rushes out to buy chocolate in the same way I do maybe you get like even a bit of a demand boost in those scenarios or a bull whip
claims.claim: Host speculation: news-driven consumer stockpiling could pull demand forward and create a bullwhip, with hidden household inventory that statistical agencies cannot see.

claims.speaker: Joe Weisenthal
claims.quote: palm oil is a tree based commodity obviously and he was describing very different market dynamics versus a field-based crop
claims.claim: Tree-based commodities have different market structure from field crops because labor intensity and difficulty of automation shape supply response.
claims.testable: no - anecdote from a palm oil businessman
